title: map / filter / reduce
description: `map`, `filter`, and `reduce` — three callbacks, three different shapes of output.

notes: All three are non-mutating — they always return a new array (or value for reduce).
Always pass an initial accumulator to `reduce`. Skipping it makes reduce throw on empty arrays.

questions.q: Which returns a new array of the SAME length as the input?
questions.explain: `map` emits exactly one output per input element; `filter` can only shrink, and `reduce` folds all the way down to a single value.

questions.q: If you forget reduce’s initial value:
options: The first element seeds the accumulator
It throws on an empty array
Both the seeding and the throw
questions.explain: Without an initial value, reduce uses arr[0] as the seed and throws on `[].reduce(fn)`.
map returns a new array; the original is untouched.

questions.q: Best tool to count elements passing a predicate:
questions.explain: All work; filter + length is the most readable.

exercises.prompt: Sum the even numbers using filter + reduce.

L3.prompt: Write `sumSqEvens(arr)` returning the sum of squares of the EVEN numbers. Log `sumSqEvens([1,2,3,4,5])`.
